items.section: 3.1 Density - Mass, volume and calculating volume
items.contents:
Language Focus:
- Key vocabulary: mass, volume, hollow, solid, regular, irregular, density and displacement.
- Comparing the mass and volume of objects and materials.
- Calculating the volume of regular objects using length × width × height.
- Finding the volume of irregular objects using water displacement.
- Comparison language: larger/smaller than, the same volume of and whereas.
- Sequence language: First, Next, Then and Finally.
Skills Focus:
- Reading
- Speaking
- Writing
items.sb:
Resources:
- Open the Teacher Guide first for the teaching flow and materials.
- Use the Student Handout during the lesson.
- Refer to Teacher Handout 3.1, pages 1-2, for source content and original activities.
- Teachers may flexibly adapt the Teacher Guide and Student Handout to suit students’ needs.

Week 1_U3.1_Mass, volume and calculating volume
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Define hollow, solid, regular, irregular and density accurately.
- Compare objects and materials using mass and volume.
- Calculate the volume of regular objects using the correct equation and unit.
- Calculate the volume of irregular objects using water displacement.
- Describe the displacement method using sequence language.
Skills:
- Reading: identify key definitions and information in Science notes and diagrams.
- Speaking: compare mass and volume and explain the correct method for finding volume.
- Writing: complete volume calculations and write a logical step-by-step method.
Value:
- Develop accuracy and logical thinking when selecting and applying methods to calculate volume.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Provide word and definition cards and keep sequence stems visible.
- Model one example for each volume method.
- Provide partially completed calculations.
Core group:
- Complete the guided notes and volume calculations independently.
- Explain one calculation orally using the correct unit.
- Compare regular and irregular volume methods.
Challenge group:
- Explain why changing the order of multiplication does not change the volume.
- Compare the advantages and limitations of the two volume methods.
items.assess:
- Getting Started responses.
- Vocabulary matching and guided notes.
- Regular-volume calculation.
- Water-displacement calculation.
- Sequenced method explanation.
- Exit Ticket.

items.section: 3.1 Density - Calculating density, comparing densities and floating
